question: If the alpha split is chosen by a bottleneck/fastest-safe rule using e-values at the fixed safety target mu0, does that automatically preserve coverage of numerical confidence bounds for an unknown true mu?

exact_counterexample.setup: Two channels, two candidate splits (.045,.005) and (.005,.045). The selector gives .045 to the channel with smaller target-evidence T_j=E_j(mu0), i.e. the apparent bottleneck. At a different true parameter theta_j, let the true-null e-value R_j=E_j(theta_j) equal 1/.045 with probability .045 and 0 otherwise, independently across channels, so E[R_j]=1 and each true-null e-value is valid. Under the true-parameter distribution, target-null evidence E_j(mu0) is not required to be an e-value because mu0 is false; define T_j=0 exactly when R_j is high and T_j=M>0 otherwise.
exact_counterexample.selector_effect: Whenever exactly one channel has the rare high true-null e-value, that channel has smaller target evidence and therefore receives alpha .045. If both are high, either tie-break still selects a high channel.
exact_counterexample.conclusion: A rule that is anti-selective/bottleneck-balancing at the safety target can still invalidate numerical confidence coverage away from that target. Evidence used for fixed-null decision routing and evidence needed for true-parameter CI coverage are not interchangeable.

interpretation: This does not show that the deployed V3 selector fails; it shows there is no general theorem from 'choose the weaker target channel' alone to strict numerical SoS coverage.

For fixed-null decision-IUT, each true null can use its own full alpha because rejecting all component nulls is an intersection-union decision. Numerical simultaneous bounds have the opposite union-of-miscoverage error geometry and require a separate reporting guarantee.
Pilot-freeze-fresh-confirm remains valid because post-freeze reporting e-processes are conditionally valid at each candidate true parameter regardless of how pilot target evidence selected the split.
scope_guards: Abstract e-value-family existence counterexample; not a fitted Bernoulli/V3 production model.
The construction exploits that E(mu0) need not be e-valid under a distribution whose true parameter differs from mu0; this is exactly the distinction relevant to numerical confidence coverage.
Do not infer a production miscoverage rate from 0.087975.
